- Provide an initial $8k credits allocation scoped to a 30-day private VPC pilot (isolated tenancy)

- Provide a simple SOW and a DocuSign path (procurement needs this to sign off)

Hi Claire — great to meet you. Short answers up front: yes we can, and we have a small conditional path we use for security-led pilots. Details below and next steps.

What we can offer now
- Conditional credit pool: $8,000 usable only in a dedicated VPC project for 30 days. Credits will be set to expire at the end of the window unless we extend via signed SOW.
- Required evidence: redacted SOC 2 Type II, runtime pen-test summary, and a brief network diagram showing VPC peering model. You sent the questionnaire already — thank you.
- Paperwork: we’ll draft a one-page SOW and a short MSAs addendum for Private deployment. DocuSign route is fine.

We do require a short security attestation (signature from your security lead) once you confirm the evidence meets your internal requirements. Typical time to provision credits after internal approvals: 24–48 hours.

Next steps I recommend:
1) I’ll loop in Ben (sales lead) to confirm credit amount and set up the credit object.
2) Laura (security/compliance counsel) will review the redacted SOC2 & pen-test summary and confirm conditional provisioning.
3) We’ll send an SOW draft and DocuSign link; Procurement can countersign.

Will proceed once Ben/Laur a confirm.

Cheers,
Jasmine Liu

- Credit usage will be monitored and constrained to the VPC project id. We’ll share token-level usage for the pilot.
- We typically require a PO or signed SOW for anything beyond 7 days of provisioning, but for security-led pilots we’ll start the credits as "provisioned pending evidence" for up to 48 hours.
- If HealthGrid needs more runway after 30 days we’ll convert to a short-term paid addendum.

Laura — can you review the redacted SOC2 and pen-test and confirm green/amber/red for provisioning? Vivek — heads up, this is the HealthGrid POC that will likely convert to a Dedicated contract if pilot goes well (region: US).

Ben / Jasmine — I reviewed the artifacts Claire uploaded (got the filled questionnaire and the redacted SOC2). Summary:

- SOC2 (redacted): acceptable for initial pilot; no severe control gaps observed in redacted report.
- Pen-test summary: need the one-page executive summary (they provided raw findings but not the sanitized summary).
- KMS/HSM note: HealthGrid requests KMS integration for key separation. We can enable customer-managed keys in the Dedicated plan; for the short pilot we can confirm a documented key handling flow and consent to a temporary escrow arrangement.

Decision: conditional provisioning green with a single condition — HealthGrid provides a one-page pen-test exec summary and signs the security attestation clause in the SOW. Once we have that, ops can flip the credit flag and provision within 24 hours.

Credit limit recommendation: $8,000 for 30 days. If HealthGrid signs the SOW within 5 business days we can consider a single 15-day grace extension at our discretion (sales to approve).

Laura Bennett
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
